The spread operator `{...item}` creates a new object on every render iteration, forcing React to treat each item as changed and preventing reconciliation optimizations.

**Fix**: Pass props individually instead of spreading:
```tsx
const renderItem = ({item}: {item: Item}) => <ItemRow id={item.id} reportID={item.reportID} value={item.value} highlight />;
```

While this is not a spread operator violation, using `.includes()` on an array inside `renderItem` is inefficient. The array lookup has O(n) complexity and runs for every item rendered in the list.

**Fix**: Convert `newTransactionIDs` to a Set before passing to child components:

In the parent component:
```tsx
const newTransactions = useNewTransactions(reportMetadata?.hasOnceLoadedReportActions, transactions);
const newTransactionIDsSet = useMemo(() => new Set(newTransactions.map((transaction) => transaction.transactionID)), [newTransactions]);
```

Then pass the Set and use `.has()`:
```tsx
shouldHighlight={newTransactionIDsSet.has(item.transactionID)}
```

This changes the lookup from O(n) to O(1) for each rendered item.

Inline style arrays `[styles.textMicroSupporting]` and `[styles.mlAuto]` create new references on every render, impacting list performance.

**Suggested fix:**
Define outside renderItem or use single style values directly:

```typescript
const textMicroSupportingStyle = [styles.textMicroSupporting];
const mlAutoStyle = [styles.mlAuto];

// Or better, use single styles directly:
<Text style={styles.textMicroSupporting}> • </Text>
<View style={styles.mlAuto}>
```

Inline style array creation in `renderItem` causes performance issues. Creating `[styles.flex2, styles.flexColumn, styles.justifyContentEvenly]` on every render creates new references, preventing React from efficiently reconciling list items.

**Suggested fix:**
Define the style array outside renderItem:

```typescript
const flex2ColumnStyle = [styles.flex2, styles.flexColumn, styles.justifyContentEvenly];

const renderItem: ListRenderItem<Transaction> = ({item}) => {
    // ...
    <View style={flex2ColumnStyle}>
```

Creating a new Badge component inline for each list item prevents React from properly reconciling the component tree. The Badge component is recreated on every render, causing unnecessary re-renders.

**Suggested fix:**
Move the Badge creation outside the data mapping loop or memoize it:

```tsx
const primaryContactBadge = useMemo(() => <Badge text={translate('domain.admins.primaryContact')} />, [translate]);

// Then in the data.push:
rightElement: primaryContact === details?.login ? primaryContactBadge : undefined,
```

Or render it conditionally in the list item component instead of creating it inline in the data structure.

`renderItem` functions execute for every visible list item on each render. Creating new objects with spread operators forces React to treat each item as changed, preventing reconciliation optimizations and causing unnecessary re-renders of child components.

Move this object creation outside of `renderItem` to the data preparation phase.
